Current clinical conditions of stiff-person syndrome in China, a
national survey
N. Xiong, J. Yang, L. Liu, J. Xiong, X. Zhang, G. Zhang, J. Huang,
T. Wang (Wuhan, China)
Objective: To survey current status and choices regarding diag-
nosis and treatment of Stiff-person syndrome (SPS) in Mainland
China.
Background: Stiff-person syndrome, the incidence, prevalence
and clinical speciality of which in mainland China remains unex-
plored. Here, we analyzed the published Chinese literature to assess
the clinical features of SPS in China.
Methods: A computer-based online search of China National
Knowledge Infrastructure was performed to review case reports con-
cerning SPS published between January 1st, 1994 and October 31st,
2012.
Results: 105 patients (68 males and 37 females) were collected
in total. The disease affects males as twice as females. All cases
were sporadic and response well to the benzodiazepine therapy. 67
patients were accurate onset with the mean onset age was 45.8 years,
axial muscles were involved in 80.6% (54/67) of these suffers while
limb muscles spasm was observed in 98.5% cases. It is noteworthy
that the involvement of brainstem muscles including throat muscle,
masticatory muscles account for 34.3% (23/67) patients during diag-
nosis and 31.3% (21/67) subjects companied other diseases such as
DM (3/67), hyperthyroidism during onset duration. EMG of 90

(85.7%, 90/105) patients presented CMUA, while only 3 of 12 (3/
12) tested subjects showed positive anti-GAD results.
Conclusions: The possibility of SPS should be considered when
come across a patient with spasm regardless of affected region and
onset course. The speciﬁc clinical manifestation and EMG with
CMUA are generally believed essential for the diagnosis of SPS. In
addition, the existence of anti-GAD body is uncommon in Chinese
suffers, and a further study of the relationship between SPS and anti-
GAD are urgently needed.
